The Caribbean & Mexico Guide: How to Choose the Right Island for the Right Trip

Six destinations. Dozens of properties. One question that matters more than any other: which version of the Caribbean are you actually looking for?

Home › Travel Journal › Destination Guide › Caribbean & Mexico
MS
Mark Sole Founder & Travel Director, Hit Your Mark Travel
Share

The Caribbean is the most misleading travel category in the world. Every brochure shows the same turquoise water and the same white sand. Every hotel Instagram looks indistinguishable from 35,000 feet. Turks & Caicos and the Dominican Republic are both Caribbean. The water in both is warm. The sand in both is white. The experience in both is as different as a quiet library and a stadium — and the price difference between the two is not always what you'd assume.

This matters because most Caribbean research leads people to the wrong place. They find a photo that looks like what they want, they find a rate that fits the budget, and they book. Then they arrive and realize the resort is larger than they imagined, the beach is more crowded than the photographs suggested, and the island itself has nothing to offer beyond the property's pool bar. Or they avoid the region entirely because "it looks too touristy," when a week at Rockhouse in Negril or a villa on Providenciales would have been exactly the trip they were looking for.

I've been planning Caribbean and Mexico travel long enough to know that the question is never which island in the abstract — it's which property, which room category, which month, and which version of the destination you're actually trying to have. This guide covers six destinations where we consistently send clients, the honest character of each, when to go, and the properties that earn their room rates. It's the framework I use before any Caribbean or Mexico booking.

Why Island Selection Is the Most Important Decision You'll Make

Most destinations in the world can be partially salvaged by a great hotel. If the city is overwhelming, you retreat to the room. If the food scene disappoints, you find the one good restaurant and go twice. The Caribbean is different because you can't retreat from the island itself. If the character of the place doesn't match what you were looking for — if you wanted quiet and got bustle, or cultural texture and got a resort zone — no amount of room upgrade fixes that.

St. Barth's is expensive not because of an arbitrary market premium but because of what the island is: small, French, without a single chain hotel, with an airport approach that requires a specific type of pilot and a clientele that comes back every year because the island earns the loyalty. The Dominican Republic's Samaná Peninsula is under-visited not because it lacks quality but because most travelers never get past the name "Dominican Republic," which has been defined in most people's minds by the mega-resort zone near Punta Cana that bears no resemblance to the rest of the country.

The goal of this guide is to give each destination an honest portrait so you can select the right one before the booking conversation begins.

"The Caribbean looks the same in every photograph. On the ground, the difference between the right island and the wrong one can be the whole trip."

Six Destinations at a Glance

Below is a breakdown of each destination — its character, who it's right for, the timing that matters, and the specific properties worth knowing. After the island portraits, I've added a timing guide and a property reference section for the region as a whole.

The Destinations
Six Islands. Six Different Trips.
01
Turks & Caicos
Top Pick Beach Purist Families
British West Indies · Providenciales
Grace Bay Beach is consistently ranked among the finest beaches in the world, and the ranking is accurate. Twelve miles of uninterrupted white sand and water that is genuinely that color in person. The island is small enough to navigate without a car, exclusive enough to feel uncrowded even at peak season, and close enough to the eastern seaboard to make a 5-night trip feel complete rather than rushed.

The correct accommodation here is a north-shore villa: three or four bedrooms, a private pool, a chef who comes in four evenings and leaves the kitchen provisioned for the others. The right charter operator gets you to the uninhabited cays north of Providenciales by mid-morning — a sandbar at high tide, a full reef at low tide, a sundowner on the water before heading back. Turks is for people who want the beach experience done as well as it can be done, without theater.
Best Months: December – April Avoid: August – October (hurricane risk) Gateway: PLS direct from JFK, MIA, BOS Key Properties: Grace Bay Club, Wymara, The Shore Club
02
St. Barth's
Couples Luxury Repeat
French West Indies · Gustavia
The most genuinely exclusive island in the Caribbean — small, French, with no chain hotels, an airport approach that requires a pilot who has done it before, and a clientele that returns every year because the island earns that loyalty. Villa stays are the correct format: a private pool, a hillside terrace above Gustavia harbor, a provisioned kitchen for the mornings when you don't want to leave.

The restaurant scene punches significantly above the island's size, and the best tables require reservations made before you arrive. The shopping in Gustavia rewards casual browsing without pressure. The water around the offshore islands is clear to the point of feeling implausible. St. Barth's is expensive for the same reason that anything exclusive is expensive — because the supply of what it offers is genuinely limited, and the demand from people who know what it is never goes away.
Best Months: December – March; April–May excellent and quieter Gateway: SXM (St. Maarten) + short hop Key Properties: Le Toiny, Rosewood Le Guanahani, Hotel Le Village St Jean
03
Jamaica
Culture Food Character
Greater Antilles · Negril · Port Antonio · Montego Bay
The most culturally specific island in the Caribbean — a place with its own music, its own food tradition, its own distinct rhythm. The right property in the right parish makes Jamaica exceptional in a way no other island delivers. The cliffs above Negril at Rockhouse, where rooms are carved into the limestone above the sea, are unlike anything else in the region. Round Hill in Montego Bay is the classic luxury estate — villas and service and a very specific clientele. GoldenEye in Oracabessa is where Ian Fleming wrote James Bond and where the setting still holds the atmosphere.

Jamaica rewards travelers who are willing to go off-property. A drive into the Blue Mountains, a jerk chicken lunch at the roadside spot the hotel guide knows by name, a morning at a fish market in a fishing village on the south coast — these are the experiences that make a Jamaica trip distinct from every other Caribbean trip you've taken.
Best Months: December – April Note: Avoid mass-resort zone near Montego Bay if culture matters Key Properties: Rockhouse Hotel, Round Hill, GoldenEye
04
Barbados & Eastern Caribbean
Honeymooners Discerning
Eastern Caribbean · Barbados · St. Lucia · Anguilla
Barbados for the west coast — the Platinum Coast has a handful of properties that have been doing luxury correctly for decades, a food scene that outperforms the island's size, and a British-Caribbean cultural overlay that gives the island a distinct character. Sandy Lane is the standard for what a Caribbean luxury hotel should feel like. Coral Reef Club and Cobbler's Cove are the boutique alternatives that deliver the same quality at a more intimate scale.

St. Lucia for the Pitons — the twin volcanic peaks that frame a beach resort in a way no flat island can replicate. Jade Mountain's open-wall sanctuaries are among the most photographed rooms in the region, and the experience justifies the photography. Anguilla for Malliouhana and the extraordinarily beautiful beach at Meads Bay, for travelers who want the Caribbean with the crowds removed entirely.
Best Months: December – April Key Properties: Sandy Lane (Barbados), Jade Mountain (St. Lucia), Malliouhana (Anguilla) Pairs With: Multi-island itineraries work well in this cluster
05
Riviera Maya & Los Cabos
Two Mexicos
Mexico · Yucatán Peninsula · Baja California Sur
Two very different versions of Mexico for two very different trips, sharing nothing but a country flag. Riviera Maya is cenotes, Mayan ruins at Tulum, a jungle that presses against the beach, and a boutique hotel category — Rosewood Mayakoba, Chablé, Azulik — that bears no resemblance to the Cancun hotel zone twenty miles north. The cultural context here is real and accessible: the cenotes feel ancient because they are, the ruins are extraordinary, and the food in Tulum and Playa del Carmen has evolved into something worth planning a meal around.

Los Cabos is the desert where the Pacific meets the Sea of Cortez — a landscape so visually specific it doesn't look like anywhere else. Private villa communities with direct beach access, deep-sea fishing at dawn, a restaurant scene that has matured significantly over the past decade, and a collection of luxury properties — One&Only Palmilla, Las Ventanas al Paraiso, The Cape — that compete with anything in the Caribbean.
Riviera Maya: Year-round (dry season Nov–May) Los Cabos: October – May (summer heat significant) Key Properties: Rosewood Mayakoba · Chablé (RM); One&Only Palmilla · Las Ventanas (Cabos)
06
Dominican Republic
Families Value Luxury
Greater Antilles · Samaná · Rio San Juan · Punta Cana
The most misunderstood destination in the Caribbean, defined in most travelers' minds by the mass-market hotel zone near Punta Cana that bears no resemblance to the rest of the country. The Dominican Republic done correctly looks like this: Amanera on a clifftop above the sea at Rio San Juan, where the Aman experience reaches the Caribbean at a fraction of the Maldives rate. The Samaná Peninsula — Las Terrenas, the whale-watching in season, the waterfalls that require a horse to reach — which still has the character of a destination the world hasn't fully discovered yet.

For families who want the all-inclusive format to work at its actual best, the right properties in the DR deliver that — strong food, genuine staff culture, and a value proposition that holds up when you're budgeting for four or six people rather than two.
Best Months: December – April Avoid: Late August – October (peak hurricane season) Key Properties: Amanera (Rio San Juan), Tortuga Bay (Punta Cana), Bahia Principe Samana
Timing
When to Go — and When to Think Twice
Dec – Mar
Peak Season
Best weather across the region. Full resort operations. Christmas and New Year's weeks book 12+ months out for top properties. Rates at their highest, but the experience is at its most complete.
Prime Window
Apr – May
Shoulder Season
Near-identical conditions to peak season. 20–30% lower rates. Noticeably fewer people at most properties and beaches. The smart choice for travelers with any flexibility in their dates.
Best Value
Jun – Aug
School Holidays
School vacation crowds increase. Building heat and humidity. Early hurricane season begins in June — insurance is important. Manageable with the right island (Aruba, southern islands are safer) and the right property.
Sep – Oct
Low Season
Lowest rates in the region. Highest hurricane risk. Some islands (Aruba, Bonaire, Curaçao, Barbados) carry significantly lower risk than the northern Caribbean. Travel insurance with cancellation coverage is essential during this window.
Properties Worth Knowing
Eight Properties That Earn Their Rates
Not a comprehensive list — these are the specific properties that consistently deliver what they promise across the Caribbean and Mexico. Organized by destination.
Grace Bay Club
Luxury Suite
Providenciales · Turks & Caicos
Suite-only property on the north shore, directly on Grace Bay. The combination of beach quality, service standard, and suite configuration makes this the right answer for couples or small groups who want Turks done at the highest level without the villa rental overhead.
Le Toiny
Villa Compound
St. Barth's · French West Indies
Fourteen hillside villas on the quieter eastern end of St. Barth's — each with a private pool, no shared beach (the east-facing water is rough), and the kind of seclusion that makes the French Caribbean worth the price. The restaurant is consistently excellent. Not for anyone seeking beach-forward resort infrastructure.
GoldenEye
Boutique Estate
Oracabessa · Jamaica
Ian Fleming's original estate on Jamaica's north coast — villas, cottages, and beach huts scattered across a protected cove where the sea grass begins. The Fleming Villa has the original study where the Bond novels were written. The reef directly offshore is exceptional. The property is genuinely immersed in Jamaica in a way that the Montego Bay resorts are not.
Jade Mountain
Sanctuary
Soufrière · St. Lucia
Open-wall sanctuaries facing directly into the Pitons — each room has no fourth wall, exposing the dramatic volcanic landscape to the room as though it were a living painting. The infinity pool at altitude. The sister property Anse Chastanet below has the beach and dive operation. The combination of the two is an itinerary within an itinerary.
Rosewood Mayakoba
Jungle Luxury
Riviera Maya · Mexico
Canal-laced jungle property between Playa del Carmen and Tulum — overwater casitas, a beach club on the Caribbean, a spa complex that takes the jungle seriously, and a golf course by Greg Norman that is incidentally very good. The property manages scale well. It is large but doesn't feel it, which is the hardest thing for a Riviera Maya resort to achieve.
One&Only Palmilla
Pacific Benchmark
San José del Cabo · Mexico
The benchmark for Los Cabos luxury — the original great property in the corridor, built on the only swimmable beach in the area. The service culture here is the product of decades of refinement. The restaurant is reliably the best meal in the corridor. The spa and beach club are both exceptional. The standard against which all other Cabos properties are measured.
Amanera
Ultra Luxury
Rio San Juan · Dominican Republic
The Aman property in the Dominican Republic, on a clifftop above the sea at Rio San Juan on the north coast — far from Punta Cana, far from anything that most people associate with the DR. Twenty casitas, a private golf course, beach access via a cliffside path, and the food and service standard that the Aman brand delivers consistently regardless of continent.
Sandy Lane
Institution
St. James · Barbados
The Platinum Coast institution — the reference point for Caribbean hotel luxury for decades. The beach is among the finest on the west coast. The food is excellent. The service culture has been refined over time to a level that is difficult for newer properties to replicate without the institutional knowledge that Sandy Lane has accumulated. Not the newest or most photographed, which is exactly the point.
